correctness.rationale: For three circular chord lengths s(alpha)=2sin(alpha/2), T is their sum minus the largest, so T<=2P/3<=2sqrt(3) with unique equilateral maximum. In the rare event delta_i=alpha_i−2pi/3=O(t), largest gap I identifies a wedge; r=delta_I, u=(delta_{I+1}−delta_{I+2})/(3r)∈[-1,1], and the exact identity T=4sin(pi/3−r/4)cos(3ru/4) gives D=2sqrt3−T=r/2+sqrt3(1+9u²)r²/16+O(r³). The cutoff r_t=2t−sqrt3(1+9u²)t²/2+O(t³), triangular-simplex density 1/(2pi²), and Jacobian 3r/2 yield P=9/(8pi²)∫r_t(u)² du=9t²/pi²−18sqrt3 t³/pi²+O(t⁴). Normalized density tends in L1 to I uniform, R density 2R and u uniform; quadratic expansion of P yields joint weak perimeter mark. Independently checked cutoff integrals at t=.01,.02. Finite integration does not prove the asymptotic.

value.rationale: The maximum-length Euclidean 3-terminal spanning tree is a natural nonsmooth geometric functional, distinct from smooth triangle perimeter and from optimal Steiner-network lengths. Its cusp changes the extreme-tail exponent and creates a new Beta/uniform conditional shape decomposition with a nontrivial quadratic perimeter scale. The result is precise and independently useful for random geometric network extremal statistics.
